_provenance.description: How the rule set was assembled and what has not been verified.

rule.description: Severity is derived from risk, not from consensus (flag-001). A rule may block only if its match is unambiguous AND the pattern is almost never wanted deliberately. Catalog count is recorded as provenance and does not affect severity.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. Appears in refusal messages and in .undercoat.local.json mutes.

severity.description: block refuses the write (exit 2). warn allows it and attaches a note.

unambiguous.description: Does the regex mean one thing? False when the match is a proxy that also fires on unrelated, legitimate code.

rarely_legitimate.description: Is this pattern almost never wanted on purpose? False when a reasonable project might deliberately want it.

risk_note.description: Required on warn rules. Says which of the two tests the rule fails and why, so the severity call is auditable.

catalogs.description: How many public catalogs independently name this pattern. Provenance only — since flag-001 this does NOT drive severity.

match.description: Python regex, searched against the content about to be written.

in.description: Glob patterns. The rule only applies to paths matching at least one.

not_in.description: Glob patterns. A path matching any of these is exempt. The primary false-alarm control.

because.description: Why this is a tell. Quoted verbatim as the WHY line in the refusal and rendered into AGENTS.md.

instead.description: The direction to go instead. Constrains without prescribing a specific replacement.

allOf.description: A rule may only block if both risk tests pass.
A warn rule must say which test it failed.
